children: Mumbai-based Oyster Renewable Energy Pvt Ltd has commissioned a 10 MW solar power project for Aster Medcity in Kerala, in partnership with Aster DM Quality Care, with the project expected to meet more than 90% of the hospital’s total energy requirement through renewable power.

The ground-mounted project, located at Ambalathara and adjoining villages in Hosdurg Taluka, Kasargod district, is expected to generate about 17.7 million units (MUs) of clean energy annually and meet more than 90% of Aster Medcity’s total energy requirement on a captive basis. The project uses high-efficiency bifacial solar modules designed for Kerala’s tropical climate. Power is supplied through Oyster Green Hybrid Two Pvt Ltd, in which Aster Group holds a 26% equity stake. Aster DM Quality Care has invested Rs 3.87 crore in the project.

Once fully operational, the project is expected to offset approximately 23,138 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually, the company stated in an official release. The project is Oyster Renewable’s second-largest solar installation for a healthcare institution, according to the company. Oyster Renewable Managing Director and CEO Siddharth Bhatia said the project has been designed to provide reliable and cost-efficient clean power for the round-the-clock energy requirements of healthcare facilities.

Oyster Renewable operates as an independent power producer focused on renewable energy solutions for commercial and industrial consumers. The company develops, invests in and operates renewable energy projects, with a focus on hybrid solar-wind systems designed to provide more consistent power supply and reduce carbon emissions.

title: Oyster Renewable commissions 10 MW solar project for Aster Medcity in Kerala
